chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Ten months in the army and signing paychecks for illiterate men
summary: He stayed ten months, joking about staying 40 like Jack Benny, and signed an X on payrolls for men who could not write.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, listen, how long did that period of your life last, how long were you there then in that camp?

It seems to be the story of my life that I've never been any place too long. They say that Aries people are something like this, but I think that if i had a good way to express myself, and didn't have to worry about the economics of life, I think I'd stay someplace perhaps -- not forever but I think I'd probably stay there for a long time. Particularly at my age now. Let's see, how old am I? I think I'm a little bit older than Jack Benny was. I'm 40. Jack Benny stayed 39 for -- is that right?
Well, I'm going to stay on 40.
Yes, right. Just a little older than Jack Benny.
On top of that such a lovely man.
Very humorous. But I stayed in the army for 10 months to be exact, you know, and while I was in the army I would go into town on my leave. You know, every-

body would get a pass on certain occasions and I'd have to say because I was the company clerk, and getting back to why the guys liked me I'm also -- before I forget it, another reason why a lot of them like me is was because many of those guys were so uneducated that they couldn't write their names.
And I had to sign an X for them on their payroll.
So they'd get their money. So I became a savior to many of those guys, and the guy that got their money for them.
